messages:
ash: Heads up — since this morning we're seeing a subtle eviction pattern in apse1: lots of tiny pods get preempted, then scheduled back repeatedly. cost metrics spiking on tiny-job queues :chart_with_upwards_trend:

jordan: same. noticed warmnodes showing as 'available' but not accepting tiny pods for ~30s then they accept a burst. looks like some handshake collision with the warmpool controller.

rachel: digging through scheduler logs. saw a repeated 'lease not granted: conflicting buffer' in the controller-manager logs. paste of tail:
```
I0312 09:14:22.123 lease_controller.go:217] attemptAcquireLease pod-alloc-xyz failed: buffer-conflict: reserved-buffer=0.65 requested=0.02
I0312 09:14:22.124 scheduler.go:990] backoff scheduling pod-alloc-xyz reason=affinity-mismatch
```

ash: ah that 'reserved-buffer' number looks like our new ghost-buffer feature from the warmnode rollout. might be overly conservative when multiple small pods hit at once.

lee: @ash @rachel can you confirm this only affects fractional tiny pods (requests < 0.05 GPU)? did we change any threshold?

jordan: yes only tiny pods. regular batch jobs fine. also seen increased node churn: nodes go from Ready->NotReady briefly then back. probably the attach/detach loops from rapid eviction.

rachel: reproducer: queue a loop of 50 tiny pod creates in apse1, watch warmnode buffer metric `warmpool/ghost_buffer_fill` — it oscillates and then the scheduler starts rejecting until it drains.

ash: short term mitigation: set warmpool.ghost_buffer_enabled=false for apse1 (flag on controller). That should lower rejection and reduce evict loop.

lee: ops checklist if we flip that: ensure we don't create burst placement hotspots that hit NVLink or NIC limits. maybe enable local throttling: `kubectl patch configmap/placement-cfg -p '{"data":{"tiny_pod_rate": "100/s"}}'`

jordan: I ran the patch in staging, decreased eviction rate by ~70% and node Ready flapping stopped. CPU on node agents stays stable.

devops-bot: Deploy start: patch placement-cfg (sha: a1b2c3) targeting apse1. Rollout window: 5m.

rachel: rolling it now to apse1 canaries (2 racks) — monitoring token-cost and preemptions.

ash: longer-term we should revisit ghost-buffer heuristics: current formula reserves buffer proportional to inflight-requests without accounting for tiny-pod multiplexing. Proposed: treat requests < 0.05 as packable and apply multiplex factor 8x. Also add a safety cap on reserved-buffer at 0.15.

lee: agree. also add telemetry: emit `ghost_buffer_conflicts_total{pod_size=\"tiny\"}` so we can alert when conflict rate > 5/min.

jordan: filed an RFC issue: /issues/ENGPLAT-2371 with the heuristic proposal and cost impact calc (est ~12% lower token bill for tiny workloads).

ash: good. for now, watch apse1 post-rollout for 30m. ping here with any regressions. :eyes:
